undeclared_returned: field_data.field_type_raw is documented as 'the raw numeric type' but is actually a string type-name ("string", "date", "dropdown", "multi_dropdown", "url"), never a number, for every custom field observed on both templates

field_data (custom fields) carries 12 keys the contract never enumerates: group_id, project_id, entity_type, default_value, is_required, is_bulk_editable, placeholder, record_status, is_filterable, parent_custom_field_id, created_at, updated_at

notes: describeCapability declares a rich, non-thin 200 schema (not a passthrough) — path_params.id (integer, required) is the only input, no query/body/json_path. Both invokes succeeded on the first attempt (no retries needed): id=1164 'Test Case Steps' and id=1664 'Test Case BDD', both real system templates from the fixture pool. Confirms the earlier batch's core facts on 1164: description_fields system ids [1,2,3,4,8,9], properties_fields system ids [10,11,12,13,14,15,16] plus exactly 30 custom field ids, and is_mandatory is false on every single mapping row on both templates (Title/Attachments/Owner/Requirements included), with field_data.optional false for those same system fields on both templates — so the 'nothing is non-removable' finding replicates across a second template, ruling out a one-record fluke. 1664 additionally carries system_field_id 5/6/7 (Background/Features/Scenario, all gherkin type) in its description_fields in place of just id 4 on 1164 — expected, since BDD templates model additional description sections; step_fields is [] on both (workspace has no step custom fields enabled), matching the contract's 'always empty array, key always present' note. New since the earlier batch: field_count is null on BOTH templates now (previously known as 45/47) — this is NOT itself a contract violation, since the schema explicitly allows field_count nullable 'when the count was not computed for this response', and get_template appears to simply never compute it (list_templates presumably does) — but it does mean the earlier-recorded 45/47 numbers should not be relied on as this endpoint's output. project_count is 1830 on both (not null), matching the 'non-null when workspace-wide count computed' branch. The real drift, and the reason for the DRIFT verdict rather than PASS: (1) the contract makes one specific, checkable claim about field_data — that field_type_raw carries 'the raw numeric type' — and this is factually wrong on every custom field in both responses; field_type_raw is always a string type-name (string/date/dropdown/multi_dropdown/url), never numeric, while the human-readable name lives in field_type (e.g. field_type: "field_string", field_type_raw: "string" — both strings, neither numeric). (2) field_data itself is left almost entirely unenumerated by the contract (just 'the underlying field definition... for custom fields the type is a name with the raw numeric type alongside it'), yet in practice it is a large, asymmetric object: system fields carry 7 keys, custom fields carry 17, including several with real semantic weight the contract never previews — notably field_data.is_required, which was true on custom field CF_x3ckvk (id 104762) on BOTH templates while the mapping-level is_mandatory for that same row was false. That is a second, more consequential thing the earlier batch's 'nothing is non-removable' framing could miss if someone only reads is_mandatory: a custom field can independently declare itself required via field_data.is_required, and the contract's field_data description gives no hint this key exists or matters for editing. Also observed (informational, not a discrepancy): the 30 custom fields are identical by custom_field_id across both templates 1164 and 1664, just with per-template mapping ids/order — these are account-wide custom fields shared across all TestCase templates, consistent with is_system templates being account-wide (project_count 1830 on both). Review & Approve fields (reviewers, review status) were absent from properties_fields on both, consistent with the contract's guidance that this surface filters them even when stored — but per that same guidance this is unverifiable proof of filtering vs. genuine absence, since we cannot see the templates' Review & Approve config from any other capability without invoking a write. No setup/prerequisite calls were needed: both template ids came straight from the fixture pool (1164, 1664) and get_template takes only the path id, so nothing else had to be built or verified first.
